title: Vendor security assessment scorecard + negotiation notes
content:
Purpose:
This is an internal working doc to consolidate the security assessment scorecard results for vendor evaluations and to capture negotiation playbook notes we can reuse during contracting. The goal: produce a repeatable grading rubric and a short set of recommended contract changes by risk bucket so SEs and legal have a one-page playbook when engaging vendors for inference-related services (hosted, dedicated, private).

Scope:
- Applies to third-party inference providers, model hosting vendors, telemetry processors, and managed-service integrators.
- Focus is on operational security, data handling for inference payloads, and vendor support/rollback commitments.

Quick summary (TL;DR):
- Use this scorecard to grade vendors on 10 criteria.
- If total score < 60% -> require strict DPA addendum + prescriptive evidence before PO.
- 60-80% -> proceed with conditional clause set + quarterly evidence review.
- >80% -> standard DPA + targeted mitigations.

Scorecard (10 criteria, weights in parentheses):
1) Data-in-transit encryption (10%) – TLS + strong ciphers, mutual TLS for private deployments.
2) Data-at-rest encryption (10%) – disk and object encryption, key management controls.
3) KMS/Key custody (10%) – customer-managed keys (CMK) available? HSM? separation of duties.
4) Residual inference data handling (15%) – retention windows, ephemeral KV cache handling, deletion guarantees.
5) Access controls & IAM (10%) – role-based controls, privileged access reviews, break-glass.
6) Subprocessor onboarding (8%) – subprocessor list, notification cadence, termination rights.
7) Observability/telemetry minimization (7%) – sampling, PII removal, retention limits for logs/traces.
8) Incident response & notification SLA (8%) – timelines, root cause evidence, customer-facing comms.
9) Change control & model provenance (7%) – change logs for model/weight updates, rollout policies.
10) Pen tests & vulnerability management (5%) – cadence, remediation SLAs, evidence of fixes.

Scoring guidance:
- Each criterion scored 0-100. Multiply by weight and sum. Round to nearest integer.
- Document evidence required for each high/medium risk item (screenshots, config exports, SOC2 sections, pen test reports, KMS policy snippets).

Sample vendor run (ACME InferenceCo) – illustrative:
- Data-in-transit: 100 (mutual TLS supported)
- Data-at-rest: 80 (AES-256 but keys managed by vendor default, CMK add-on possible)
- KMS/custody: 60 (CMK available for enterprise customers after onboarding)
- Residual data handling: 50 (standard deletion policy 90 days; no ephemeral KV guarantee)
- IAM: 85 (fine-grained RBAC + audit logs)
- Subprocessors: 70 (list provided but no automated notification)
- Observability minimization: 40 (full traces retained 180 days)
- Incident response: 75 (48h notification, but limited forensic evidence commitment)
- Change control/model provenance: 55 (internal release notes, no signed provenance)
- Pen tests: 90 (recent pen test and remediation list)
- Total = compute weighted sum -> ~72% (conditional approval)

Risk buckets and suggested contract language (playbook):
- Critical (any criterion scored < 40 OR residual data handling < 60):
  - Require immediate DPA addendum: explicit no-retention for inference inputs unless customer enables logging; enforce ephemeral KV cache or certified deletion within X hours; right-to-audit for deletion proofs.
  - Contract clause snippets to propose to Legal:
    "Vendor shall not retain customer inference payloads or model outputs beyond the operational time required to serve the request, except as expressly authorized in writing by Customer. When caching is used, Vendor shall ensure ephemeral caches are scrubbed and key material destroyed within 24 hours of request completion; upon Customer request Vendor shall provide deletion evidence within 72 hours."
  - Require on-site or remote audit rights (quarterly evidence) and escrow of telemetry subsets if dispute arises.

- High (any criterion 40–59 OR KMS not customer-managed):
  - Proposed clauses:
    "Vendor shall, at Customer's election, support Customer-managed cryptographic keys in a manner consistent with NIST SP 800-57; if CMK is not used, Vendor shall provide written justification and compensating controls."
  - Add requirement for tighter telemetry retention (30 days) and monthly compliance attestations.

- Medium (60–79):
  - Proposed clauses: quarterly compliance snapshot and SOC2/ISO attestation uploads; a detailed incident playbook and commitment to 72-hour root-cause analysis and customer impact summary.

- Low (>=80):
  - Standard DPA with limited addenda (data minimization schedules and agreed SLAs).

Negotiation tactics / playbook notes for SEs and Legal:
- Start with the scorecard facts: present the weighted score and 2–3 prioritized gaps. Use evidence artifacts (screenshots, config excerpts).
- Always push for CMK for production/private deployments; for Hosted POCs we can accept vendor-managed keys with compensating controls and short retention windows.
- If vendor resists deletion clauses, trade for stronger logging/forensics and a shorter retention window rather than indefinite retention.
- For subprocessor concerns, require a step-in clause: Vendor must notify customer of new subprocessors 30 days before onboarding and provide a right to object for substantiated security risks.
- Use escalation path: SE -> Solutions Eng -> Security -> Legal. Keep negotiations to 2 rounds for commercial friction items; anything beyond requires GTM approval.

Suggested redlines (literal snippets to copy/paste):
- Deletion evidence clause:
  "Within 72 hours of Customer request, Vendor will provide verifiable deletion evidence (log export with deletion events and key rotation confirmations) for the specified Customer data, or a written explanation if deletion cannot be completed, together with a remediation plan."

- Subprocessor notification clause:
  "Vendor shall maintain a current subprocessor register and shall notify Customer at least thirty (30) days prior to engaging any new subprocessor that will process Customer Data. Customer may object to the new subprocessor within fifteen (15) days of notice for reasonable security or regulatory grounds. Vendor shall not use the subprocessor for Customer Data pending resolution."

- Ephemeral cache clause:
  "Vendor shall implement ephemeral KV cache protections for Customer requests. Ephemeral cache entries containing Customer Data must be encrypted with transient keys and purged within twenty-four (24) hours of creation; persistent backups shall not contain Customer inference payloads or outputs."

Evidence & onboarding checklist (attachments we ask for during review):
- Recent SOC2 Type II report (if available) or ISO 27001 cert.
- Pen test report (last 12 months) and remediation log.
- Sample IAM policy and list of roles with entitlements.
- KMS architecture diagram and policy excerpt for key rotation.
- Data retention settings for logs/tracing and cache TTLs.
- Subprocessor register export (CSV) and typical notification email template.

Open questions for vendor call (prep bullet list):
- Do you provide an ephemeral-KV option? If yes, can you demonstrate deletion logs?
- Can keys be customer-managed for dedicated/private deployments? Any additional cost?
- What is your default retention for telemetry, traces, and request logs? Can we opt into shorter retention?
- Do you accept contractual deletion-evidence obligations and a 72-hour SLA for deletion evidence?
- Are change logs and model provenance accessible by customers in a signed/immutable format?

Example negotiation timeline (target):
- Week 0: Scorecard run + request evidence.
- Week 1: Vendor call to clarify gaps.
- Week 2: Legal sends redlines for critical clauses.
- Week 3: Final commercial/legal review and approval or CISO sign-off if >2 critical gaps.

Notes & institutional memory (things we've learned):
- Vendors often claim "no retention" but default telemetry backends retain traces for 90–180 days. Always ask for concrete retention settings and proof.
- CMK is a strong differentiator; many vendors gate CMK behind enterprise plans which adds cost/time. Budget for this in procurement.
- Ephemeral KV cache is frequently the weak link for inference vendors; engineering teams must insist on an option or compensating controls.

Action items (owner assigned):

- Diego: create a vendor onboarding checklist in GH ticket JIRA-SEC-7821 and attach required evidence list. Due 2025-02-18.

Appendix: quick copy-paste negotiation snippets (for SEs)
- "For production we require either customer-managed keys or a documented compensating control with KMS rotation logs and a maximum 30-day retention on plaintext telemetry."
- "We cannot accept indefinite retention of inference inputs/outputs. Please propose a technical and contractual solution for scrub/deletion within 24-72 hours."

End of doc.

Notes to self (informal):
